title: Sweetgum, grown from buds
reads: At the page camera (ortho, turn 14, tilt 52): a young tree taller than wide, an open crown of star leaves on upright limbs that rise from a low fork, over root flares into the soil.
fits: Grown pieces: young broadleaf trees with spiral leaves and a terminal bud, as scenery.
wrong_for: Hard-surface props, rigged characters, and anything whose shape is not a branching tree.

references.gives: Krinard & Johnson 1985, Tree Planters' Notes 36(3): 6-8: planted sweetgum (10 x 10 ft) on the DEF site was 1.5, 5.8 and 12.7 ft tall after 1, 3 and 6 years (27.1 ft at 6 years on the better HP site)
NC State Extension: 60-100 ft tall, 40-50 ft spread; pyramidal, spreading; rapid growth
Gilman et al., UF/IFAS ST358: 60-75 ft tall, 35-50 ft spread; crown pyramidal, oval; grows in a narrow pyramid; typically one trunk
Virginia Tech dendrology: the terminal bud is large; leaves 4 to 6 inches across with 5 to 7 lobes, star-like; crown pyramidal, especially when young
Okabe 2016: spiral leaf arrangements sit near the golden angle, 137.5 deg

Chianucci et al. 2018 leaf inclination data: Liquidambar styraciflua blade angle mean 69.43 deg, SD 12.58, n 91; beta on t = 2 theta / pi by the method of moments a 6.1932, b 1.8352 (a reference sweep)
Demol et al. QSM trees (beech and ash): branch angles from the parent with medians of 44 to 54 deg; other species, a stand-in
